outlook: Soybeans extended their slide at midday, with November beans down about 23 cents to a two-month low after Lula's surprise win in Brazil's election knocked the Brazilian real down roughly 7%, which can make Brazilian soybeans cheaper for export buyers; China is estimated to have bought about 19 of the 25 million tonnes of U.S. soybeans it pledged. December corn was off about 2 cents under harvest pressure; USDA corrected processing errors in September's Kansas and Nebraska corn estimates, raising the September national yield to 178.8 bu/acre while leaving October's 181.2 unchanged. Wheat was lower with corn and beans: Minneapolis spring wheat fell about 8 cents and is on track for a tenth straight lower close, and Chicago wheat lost about 10 cents as Black Sea peace-deal talk continues without real progress. ICE canola eased early with the weaker soy complex.
